resources.string: This program was developed to help people with school subjects, especially with foreign languages and biology.\n\nFor any further help contact me at litos@tuta.io

Chapters are created from the floating New button inside a container: press the button and drag onto the chapter icon, or tap the icon in the standing palette. \nThey have only the basic information described above.

Every item is created from the floating New button at the bottom right. On the subjects screen it opens the subject creator right away; inside a container it fans out a circular palette of the offered types — drag the finger onto an icon, or tap the icon after a plain tap leaves the palette standing. A tap outside the icons closes the palette. 
The button hides when the list scrolls down and returns when it scrolls back up. 
All the creator dialogs have two columns for name of the new item and for its description (optional). 
The description of the item can be multiline. 
After you are done with these two colums, there can be more stuff for each different type of item. 
When you are done with all that information, click 'OK' to create the item, or click 'Cancel' to exit the dialog. A click outside the window closes the dialog too, but only when nothing was changed.
Subjects are created from the floating New button on the subjects screen — the tap opens the creator directly. \nThey have just the basic information described above.

Notes are created from the floating New button inside a container, like chapters. \nThey carry only the basic information described above — a name and a description — and serve for any text that is not a word, like a grammar rule.

Words are created from the floating New button inside a container, like chapters. 
Other than the basic information they contain an add icon below the fields, which adds a translate item. 
Translates consist of name and optional description. 
To remove a translate, click on the cancel icon on the right of the specified translate.
This application has some more functions that can sometimes help. Here is the list and explanation of them.

A subject folder of the old app version can be imported on the subjects screen: pick \'Legacy subject folder\' in the \'Import\' submenu of the \'more\' menu. \nA subject with the same name is not imported twice.

A subject can be created from a words file: on the subjects screen pick \'File\' in the \'Import\' submenu of the \'more\' menu. \nThe new subject is named after the picked file and its content is parsed exactly like the words import (chapters and words), only at the top level of the subject.

If you have similar names of certain words, and they have identical translations, combine them using these: /(). 
Slash character signals two different options ending by a whitespace, an interpunction character or a bracket. 
Examples: 
I/They come = 'I come' or 'They come' 
(I go)/(He goes). = 'I go.' or 'He goes'.

Pick an option in the \'Export\' submenu of the \'more\' menu: selected rows are exported, and with nothing selected the whole open container (every subject on the subjects screen). \nThe word file is compact and carries only the structure of the vocabulary — no success rates, no references; the JSON file is a complete replica of the subject, success rates, notes and references included. \nOnly the JSON file imports back without loss.

Words are imported through the 'more' menu — inside a container pick 'Import', on the subjects screen pick 'File' in the 'Import' submenu; inside a container they land in it, on the subjects screen they create a new subject. The import detects the file itself by its content: a file starting with '[' or '{' is a subject tree (chapters, words, notes and references), anything else is a word list. The word file can be structured in a simpler hierarchy: it can contain chapters and words. 
Description to individual items can be written directly behind the item in format like '[description]'. 
Words and translates can be separated using ';', '=', or '→'. 
Words with same translate are separated by a backward slash '\'. 
Chapters begin on a separate line in the following format 'chapter name [optional description] {', end them with a single '}' on a separate line. 
Every item should be written on a new line, spacing and indentation between them is ignored - meant only for better readability. 
Possible format example: 

chapter-in-file 1 { 
	word 1;translate 1 
	word 2=translate 2 
	subchapter name [subchapter description] { 
		word 3 [description] = translate 3 
		word 4\word 5;translate 4 
		word 6 [description] \ word 7 → translate 5 
	} 
	word 7;translate 1 [description]\translate 6 
}

Searching is enabled in all chapters and subjects. \nIn a search list, a click on a found chapter opens its container. \nThere are various methods for searching, the search engine accepts naming syntax.

"Description
a, b, or c
Any character except a, b, or c
a through z or A through Z, inclusive
a through d, or m through p: [a-dm-p]
d, e, or f 
a through z, except for b and c: [ad-z]
a through z, and not m through p: [a-lq-z]"
Regex Quantifiers \nThe quantifiers specify the number of occurrences of a character.
Regex Metacharacters \nThe regular expression metacharacters work as shortcuts.

"Description
Any character
Any digits ([0-9])
Any non-digit ([^0-9])
Any whitespace character ([\t\n\x0B\f\r])
Any non-whitespace character ([^\s])
Any word character ([a-zA-Z_0-9])
Any non-word character ([^\w])
A word boundary
A non word boundary"

"Description
X occurs once or not at all
X occurs once or more times
X occurs zero or more times
X occurs n times only
X occurs n or more times
X occurs at least y times but less than z times"

This application has more search methods aside from simple text. 
The prefix syntax has 3 levels and is initiated by '\' char followed by 0-3 modifiers and comparing value, the levels are: 
1. Level: desired type 
	W - must be a word 
	T - must be a translate 
	C - must be a chapter 
2. Level: what is compared 
	S - amount of successes 
	F - amount of fails 
	N - times tested 
	R - success rate in % 
	D - the description (if any) 
	default - name of the item 
3. Level: desired condition 
 -for text: 
	\ - contains the expression ignoring case 
	c - contains the expression 
	s - starts with the expression 
	e - ends with the expression 
	r - matches the regular expression 
 -for number value: 
	> - must be higher than the given value 
	< - must be lower 
	= - must be equal to the value 

Examples: 
	\WD	- all words with some description 
	\R>50	- items with success rate above 50% 
	\sD 	 - items starting with 'D' 
	\C\K72	- all chapters with name containing 'k72'
Permanently deletes the selected items after accepting the delete-check dialog.

Only one item can be edited at a time. A window with parameters of the selected item pops up. The style of the editing window is same as when creating that type of item. \nClick the \'OK\' button to save the changes when done editing.

All created objects can be modified in some way. 
A long-press on an item starts the select mode: the item becomes selected and the bottom sheet with possible actions shows. A tap on the checkbox of a row toggles its selection too. 
Keep the finger pressed and move it over the list to select the range of items it crosses. 
While items are selected, the search button in the top right corner becomes the select-all toggle: it selects all items of the list, or (if all items are selected) exits the selection mode. The back key also exits the selection mode. 
The list of possible actions follows below.

Cuts all selected items and shows the paste sheet (cancel and paste buttons). After you open the target chapter, click \'Paste\'. \nThe armed move survives switching chapters, the side swipe included — the swipe only cancels the row selection.

The test asks for the words of the chosen sources. 
You can choose the test's length and number of tested items. 
The switch on the test screen turns the direction around: the translations are shown and the word is answered, or the other way. 
The test can only contain items from one subject.

After the time is up or you finished the test a window with the test\'s success rate and all tested items. \nEvery item shows the word with its valid translations, how many times it was tested, its success rate (successful/total) and your answer.

After pressing the button 'Start' the test is started and the remaining time can be seen in the top. 
When you are done with the test click 'Done' to submit the test. 
You are alerted in the last 30 seconds. 
Each item has a field for the name/translation to fill in. 
Whenever you decide to abolish the test press twice the back button.

The variety of items to create the test from can be added to using the \'Add source\' button. \nThen a item chooser pops up, where you can repeatedly select items for the test (but only from on one subject). \nA test can also be prepared straight from the explorer: select the rows to test and tap \'Test\' on the selection bar.
